title: soc2-prep-scratchpad-noah-rivera
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for SOC2 readiness mapping and open questions

High-level notes:
- Working through common gaps: evidence collection for automated config drift, proof of least-privilege for service accounts, and control for third-party access.
- Goal: get to a minimal set of evidence artifacts per control that auditors accept (config snapshots, runbooks, AD / Okta reports, Splunk/Datadog alerts).

Open questions / assumptions:
- Q1: For CC6 (logical access) do auditors accept Okta system reports + AWS CloudTrail + a monthly access review (spreadsheet + Confluence notes)? Or do they want an automated access review tool output?
  - Assumption: monthly manual review is okay if documented and signed-off by manager. Follow up with auditor (Alyssa R. from audit firm).
- Q2: What level of detail for change management evidence? ticket + PR + deploy artifact + post-deploy smoke test logs?
  - Best-practice suggested: ticket link (Jira), linked GitHub PR, build artifact hash from CI, and monitoring incident check (no regressions).
- Q3: Backup restore tests frequency: quarterly restores of key DBs and object storage. Need schedule and runbooks.

Control mapping (rough):
- CC1: Risk assessment / governance
  - Evidence candidates: SOC2 program charter (Confluence), quarterly risk register (sheet), OKRs showing owner assignment.
- CC2: Access provisioning / deprovisioning
  - Evidence: Okta user lifecycle reports, JIRA onboarding/offboarding tickets, service account inventory (sheet), last 3 months of access revocations.
- CC3: Change management
  - Evidence: Jira ticket + PR + CI build log + release notes entry. Tag: INFRA-CHG-*.
- CC4: System configuration / hardening
  - Evidence: automated config scans (inspec/chef/terraform), AMI bake logs, GCP/AWS config snapshots.
- CC5: Logging & monitoring
  - Evidence: CloudTrail, Datadog/Splunk dashboards exported, alert history for critical detectors, runbook linking alerts -> incident tickets.
- CC6: Encryption & key mgmt
  - Evidence: KMS key policies, HSM usage notes (for Private customers), disk encryption status report.
- CC7: Incident response
  - Evidence: IR plan (Confluence), post-incident reports for last 12 months, tabletop exercise notes.

Immediate gaps I've observed:
- No centralized service-account inventory with owners and last-used timestamps (big gap for access control evidence).
- Change mgmt evidence is inconsistent: some repos have nicely linked Jira/PRs, others only PRs. Need enforcement (repo template + CI check).
- Lack of documented quarterly backup restore runs for PG clusters in dedicated deployments.
- Need to formalize vendor risk: standard vendor questionnaire and attestations for top 10 3P vendors.

Action items / next steps (owners):
- Inventory: build service-account inventory (sheet) with last-used metric. Owner: Priya Patel. Ticket: JIRA-INFRA-3011. Due: 2025-12-05.
- Change mgmt enforcement: add PR template + CI check that requires Jira ticket ID in PR description. Owner: Ethan Brooks. PR stub: infra#987 (linked). Due: 2025-11-30.
- Backup restore runbooks + schedule for PG clusters (Dedicated): owner: Lena Morales. Evidence: runbook export + restore logs. Due: 2025-12-15.
- Reach out to auditor (Alyssa R.) on each of Q1/Q2 above and capture answer in Confluence page. Owner: Noah Rivera. Slack: #security-soc2. Due: 2025-11-18.
- Vendor questionnaire: draft standard template and circulate. Owner: Legal + Security. Due: 2026-01-10.

Notes from quick sync with Priya (11/15):
- Priya: can pull Okta monthly login report and generate CSV of active accounts + last auth. She thinks we can script last-used checks for service principals by scanning CloudTrail and GCP audit logs.
- Action: Priya to create an initial CSV and drop in /shared_drives/security-and-compliance/evidence/soc2/ (we should confirm path with SSO team).

Evidence collection strategy (pragmatic):
- Prioritize automated sources (logs, config management, CI artifacts). Use manual artifacts (spreadsheets, signed PDFs) only where automation is costlier than the risk.
- Keep an "evidence index" Confluence page listing each control -> evidence artifact(s) + location + owner + retention policy.

Potential auditor friction points to pre-empt:
- Inconsistent tagging of infra changes across repos -> fix with templates + CI enforcement.
- Lack of owner for service accounts -> assign owner in inventory, require rota for review.
- Private deployment evidence: customers running private/on-prem have their own controls; we need a clear mapping of which company controls cover Redwood-managed infra vs customer-managed infra. Add a column in evidence index: "responsibility (Redwood vs Customer)".

Random TODOs / scratch ideas:
- Create a lightweight script to snapshot required evidence each week (Okta report, CloudTrail tail, recent PRs with Jira IDs). Might live as a GitHub Action in infra repo.
- Draft email template for asking managers to sign monthly access reviews.
- Collect last 12 months of incident postmortems and mark which are relevant for IR control evidence (tag them).

References / links to copy into Confluence: 
- Confluence: SOC2 Program Overview (linked above)
- Jira filters: "project = INFRA AND labels = soc2" (save filter for audits)
- Slack: #security-soc2 thread: "SOC2 evidence collection plan" dated 2025-11-10

Risks / mitigation notes:
- Risk: Evidence sprawl -> Mitigation: evidence index + weekly snapshot + retention policy.
- Risk: Owner fatigue for manual reviews -> Mitigation: limit manual tasks, automate where possible, rotate reviewer schedule.

Meeting notes / quick log:
- 2025-11-12: Kickoff w/ security team; agreed to build evidence index and prioritize access and change mgmt controls first.
- 2025-11-15: Sync w/ infra (Priya + Ethan) to scope automation for Okta + PR/Jira enforcement.
- 2025-11-20: Audit kickoff w/ Alyssa (tentative). Need to confirm auditor requirements by 11/18.

Bottom line / thesis:
- Focus on making evidence reproducible and automated. Auditors accept manual artifacts but those are brittle. If we can show consistent automated exports (Okta, CloudTrail, CI artifacts) + human-reviewed signoffs for exceptions, we should be in a good place.

Quick contacts:
- Alyssa R. (audit firm) 
- Priya Patel (infra)
- Ethan Brooks (infra)
summary: Working scratchpad for SOC2 prep: control mapping, open questions for auditor, action items with owners, and evidence collection plan. Prioritize access + change mgmt automation and build an evidence index.
